config.hint: The engine applies these settings itself. target: single needs one target, self is only on yourself, none has no target. range: metres, unset means unlimited. visible: True means the target must be perceived by the user. requires: a condition that must hold. noise: metres; other players within it sense the use. cast_time / cooldown: minutes. shape: area shape, e.g. sphere(radius=5), cone(length=10, angle=60), capsule(length=20, width=2), box(length=, width=, height=). placement: a trap or ward, e.g. placement(radius=3, perceive=0.5, charges=1, duration=60, notify=True). Values may be formulas using this.column other settings or the script's variables (e.g. noise = range * 2), without loops; None means unset.

g.presets_hint: Rows filled in from the header above, so players don't write them; entries players write are extra rows. When the condition is true the entry appears on the sheet and its effects apply; otherwise it doesn't appear. Conditions may only use this sheet's fields; text values need quotes, e.g. class == "warrior", class != "warrior" or class == "warrior" and str >= 3. Fixed entries don't count toward the min/max above.

rules.groups_hint: A group is one kind of entry on the sheet, such as class skills, personal skills or special abilities; make one group per kind. Each entry under it is one specific skill or ability. Entries come from two places: players add their own when creating a character, and you can write fixed entries here (optionally with a condition, e.g. only for one class).

gt.empty: No entries yet. Use “+ Row” below.
gt.hint: This kind of entry is a table: each row is an entry written by the rules (e.g. one skill), each column is something every entry fills in. Condition, Name and Description come with every row; “+ Column” adds one (e.g. rank, mana cost, damage), and clicking a column name edits its name and type. The “Script” button opens the entry's skill script in the IDE on the right; the ⤢ next to a formula cell opens it there too. Modifiers and area shapes are under the row's “More”. Conditions may only use this sheet's fields, e.g. class == "warrior"; empty means always. Row order matters: modifiers on one value run top to bottom. Players fill the same columns for their own entries.
gt.id_hint: English ID, needed to refer to this entry in formulas: hero.fireball is whether it exists (1 or 0), hero.fireball.level is its level column. Must be unique on a sheet.
gt.player_fills: Empty: the player fills it in
gt.player_fills_hint: A column left empty on a fixed entry is filled in by each player when making the character (e.g. each one's own level). If the column is required, it must be filled whenever the entry applies.
gt.script_bad: The skill script has problems; click to see
gt.script_empty: No skill script yet; click to write one in the IDE
gt.script_ok: Open the skill script in the IDE
gt.timing_hint: Cast time and cooldown are in minutes and may be formulas (24*60 is a day). Under 1 minute is instant; an action using the skill takes at least the cast time. Cooldown: after a use (hit or not) the skill can't be used again for this long.
gt.title: Entry table

help.appearance: Appearance: the player describes how the character looks. When others first see the character, its handle (e.g. "woman in a red scarf") is generated from this. It can't be removed or retyped.
help.can_fly: Can fly: ticked by the player, off by default. Flyers travel in a straight line at fly speed; others go up or down first and then along the ground at move speed. It can't be removed or retyped.
help.concealment: Multiplies how far others can notice this character: 1 is normal, 0.3 means others must be much closer. The default 1 is fine.
help.fly_multiplier: How many times the move speed a flyer flies. Default 1. Only matters for characters who can fly.
help.fly_speed: Metres per minute when flying; default fly_multiplier * move_speed. Only matters for characters who can fly.
help.hear_distance: How far (in metres) this character hears people talking. Bystanders within this range of either speaker hear the whole conversation, relayed by the keeper. Required, e.g. 30 * hear_multiplier. Walls are ignored.
help.hear_multiplier: Hearing multiplier, default 1. Skills and statuses can modify it (e.g. keen ears ×2); use it in the hearing range formula.
help.hp: HP: every kind of character must have it, as a runtime value. Its limits, initial value and change per minute can be edited; its name, kind and class can't. Damage comes off shield first (if there is one), then HP.
help.move_speed: Metres per minute. Required, e.g. 80 for an ordinary person, or 60 + agi * 2.
help.perception_radius: How far (in metres) this character notices others. Required, e.g. 50 + per, or a constant like 100.

ins.groups: Learns the entries in the subject's groups:
ins.when_hint: Worked out on the observer; target.<name> reads the subject; empty = always

rules.insights_hint: When an observer sees (or senses) a subject, the engine tells the observer's player these things from the subject's sheet and records them as intel; it tells again when a value changes. Everything else is judged by the KP from what players see, hear and find out, a little at a time.

kind_help.boolean: Yes/no: a checkbox, e.g. can fly. It's 1 or 0 in formulas.
kind_help.formula: Dice formula: a formula that may roll dice, e.g. a skill's damage 1d str, or dice(this.level, lookup(table, this.level)). In a group each entry fills its own and may use this.<column>. In the skill script and this entry's other formulas, this.<that column> uses the formula (rolled then), e.g. the script target.damage(this.damage).
kind_help.param: Chosen on use: a number the player picks each time the skill is used, e.g. how much mana to spend. Not filled at character creation; the player says it in the action and the keeper passes it to the engine when rolling. Min and max are formulas that may use the character's fields and this.<column>. With a resource to spend from, the engine checks there is enough and deducts it when the round resolves. Dice formulas refer to it as this.<column name>, e.g. (1d4 + int) * floor(30 / this.mp_spent).
kind_help.resource: Resource: a value that gets spent or restored (HP, mana, shield, uses left). The maximum may be a formula such as hp_max; empty means no limit.
kind_help.text: Text: descriptions such as background; with choices, the player picks one of them.

rules.levels_hint: Checked in order; the first true condition wins. Variables: roll, target, difficulty, opp_roll, opp_target.
rules.locked: Required by the engine; can't be changed
rules.order_matters_presets: Note: the order of fixed entries matters; effects on the same value run top to bottom.

p.what: One row of the table, i.e. one concrete entry (e.g. one skill). Name and description come with every row; each box further down is one column you added in the header above.

ph.choices: e.g. red, blue, green (comma-separated; leave empty for free text)
ph.choices_number: e.g. E=1, D=2, C=3, B=4, A=5, EX=10, or 1~5, 10 (empty for any number)
ph.choices_param: e.g. no=0, yes=1; one of these is chosen on use, the first if not said
ph.damage_taken: e.g. max(0, amount - 5 * anti_magic) if kind == "magic" else amount; empty = take it as is
ph.max_resource: e.g. hp_max; empty means no limit
ph.per_minute: empty means none, e.g. 1 or con / 2
ph.search: e.g. 1d20 + per; empty = can't find hidden ones
ph.stealth: e.g. 10 + 5 * ceil(distance / 40) if distance <= 200 else 999; empty = never hides
ph.table_rows:
One per line: key,value
e.g. warrior,14

rules.pick: Choose a rule pack and version…
rules.player_entities: Entities each player creates (template, min, max)
rules.player_entities_hint: Which kinds of character each player creates, and how many of each.
rules.problems: {n} problems; can't save a version yet (drafts are always fine)
rules.rules_text: Rules text (free text for the keeper)
rules.rules_text_hint: Rules text for the keeper: everything the pack can't express as formulas.
rules.samples_hint: Checked on save: every example must produce the expected derived values.

t.damage_taken_hint: Each time a character of this template takes skill damage, the engine uses this to work out how much (never below 0). amount is the raw damage, kind its type (from the skill's group, or damage(amount, "type")). Resistances written here apply to every attack.
t.label: Shown to players as
t.name: Template ID
t.on_death_hint: Runs the moment a character of this template dies (same syntax as skill scripts). self is the dead one, target whoever hurt it last, partners by template name (e.g. companion.set(fading, 1)).
t.stealth_hint: Stealth is worked out on this character: what someone distance metres away must roll to notice it (observer.<name> reads the observer's sheet); 0 means not hiding. Search is the roll this character makes to notice others. At the start of each round every observer that can see a hider it hasn't found rolls once; once found it stays found until out of sight. Using a skill on someone reveals you to them; a target that hasn't noticed its attacker can't react.

table.bad_rows: Line {lines} can't be read and isn't saved: write key,value with a number value

rules.tables_hint: One row per line: key,value. Range tables take the largest key not above the input; exact tables need an exact match.
rules.template_hint: A template is the format of one kind of character sheet, not a specific character: players fill a sheet from it. One template is enough if every player has the same kind of sheet; add a second if each player also controls, say, a companion. The ID is an internal code (lowercase letters, digits, underscores, e.g. hero); the label is what players see. The default character works as is.
rules.unsaved: Unsaved changes; a draft is saved automatically

uses.description: What this use does (with no config or script, the KP rules on it from this text)
uses.hint: An entry can be used in several ways (e.g. a weapon swung normally, or unleashed); each use is a skill, named “entry/use”. A use's config falls back to the entry's; this.<column> in its script is the entry's column.
uses.kp_rules: Ruled by the KP from the text
uses.name: Use name
uses.templates_hint: Use templates: players adding uses to their own entries can copy one of these (e.g. a standard area blast) and adjust it.
uses.title: Uses

wb.fix_first: Fix the problems before saving a version (drafts can always be saved)

script.hint: When the skill is used and the keeper rules it took effect (hit), the engine runs it line by line; otherwise only the cost is paid. self is the user, target is whoever it's used on (the player chooses, may be themselves); with no target only the self lines run. Actions: damage(amount) – shield first, then hp; add(field, amount[, minutes]) – with minutes it's timed and the rest is taken back when it ends; sub(field, amount); set(field, amount); modify(derived, new-value formula, minutes) – a timed modifier: the derived value's own name is the bearer's value, other names are the user's at the time of use. Amounts are formulas and may roll dice; this.column is this entry's column (dice-formula columns roll), self.x and bare names are the user's, target.x the target's, target.template the target's template name. Branches: the indented lines under if condition: run only when it holds; elif condition: and else: may follow. Conditions are worked out when the use is declared and can't roll dice; with no target, a block whose condition asks about target is skipped. Tab indents; Enter keeps the indent. # starts a comment.
script.title: Skill script (on use)

state.patch_hint: Edits are validated like adjudications and logged as admin overrides.

talk.hint: Talking happens face to face and is heard at once. While any conversation is open the round won't resolve; talking takes no game time.
talk.invited_me: @{label} wants to talk to you. If you accept, what you were doing stops and you'll act again after the talk.
talk.none: No conversation. Use Talk next to someone in the map tab's “Currently perceived” list.
